title: Client Launch Playbook - First 90 Days
content:
Purpose
This playbook is a pragmatic, action-oriented template for Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to run a repeatable, measurable client launch for the first 90 days after contract signature. It’s intended for small-to-medium deployments of Redwood Inference (hosted or dedicated) and emphasizes fast time-to-value, clear adoption milestones, and early risk detection to inform renewal conversations.

Audience
Primary: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Onboarding Specialists
Secondary: RevOps, Support, Customer Engineering, Product (for escalations)

Executive summary (one-liner)
Run a 90-day launch that converts an initial integration into predictable usage by aligning business outcomes, engineering delivery, and operational readiness — with weekly checkpoints and clear escalation triggers.

Success criteria (what success looks like at day 90)
- Business outcome: Customer has a production workload running on Redwood with measurable signal (e.g., X API calls/day or Y embeddings/min) and can demonstrate the feature driving user or revenue impact.
- Engineering outcome: Integration latency and error rates meet the agreed SLOs; can sustain baseline throughput in dedicated or hosted environment.
- Operability: Basic dashboards/live alerts in Console configured; ownership and runbook assigned.
- Renewal signal: Customer is at least NPS-neutral or above and signals willingness to expand or renew.

Primary metrics to track (weekly)
- Active traffic (requests/day)
- Successful responses (%), 95th latency (ms)
- Token consumption per session
- Feature adoption (edges using inference calls / total eligible sessions)
- Time to first production inference (days)
- Support tickets and severity trend

Stakeholder map (recommended attendees for main checkpoints)
- Customer-side: Technical lead, Product owner, Dev lead, Security/infra contact (if private)
- Redwood: CSM (owner), Solutions Engineer (integration), Onboarding Specialist, Support engineer (as escalation), Account Exec (commercial signals)

90-day plan overview (high-level cadence)
- Day 0–7: Kickoff + quick wins
- Day 8–30: Integrate + QA + early ramp
- Day 31–60: Stabilize + feature enablement + cost optimization
- Day 61–90: Scale + business review + renewal primer

Detailed timeline and playbook (play-by-day ranges)
Days 0–7: Kickoff & fast-path value
- Kickoff meeting (≤48 hours post-signature): runbook, goals, timeline, success metrics, communications cadence. Capture task owners and access needs.
- Quick win proof: demo a minimal end-to-end flow (sample app or Postman collection) using customer test data or sanitized sample.
- Access checklist: API keys, network allowlists, KMS/HSM integration notes, any VPC/VPN info for private deployments.
- Deliver: Integration checklist (shared Google Sheet), sample prompts and expected outputs, initial dashboard link.

Days 8–30: Integration and QA
- Daily stand for first 2 weeks with dev lead (or alternate cadence): unblock technical issues, prioritize bugs.
- Observability: Set up per-route dashboards, token cost heatmap, and error alerts in Console. Aim to catch regressions early.
- Performance baseline: Run synthetic load tests to characterize latency and KV cache behavior at target sequence lengths.
- Security review: Confirm logging/PII redaction, audit log access, and encryption keys are in place.
- Deliver: Integration status report (go/no-go for pilot).

Days 31–60: Stabilize and optimize
- Canary rollout: If using Redwood routes/rollouts, configure canary at 5–20% traffic, monitor quality regressions and latency.
- Cost optimization: Apply batching and caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize; consider quantized model variant for non-critical routes.
- Eval set: Run a small eval suite (20–50 prompts) to capture quality regressions and track a baseline quality score.
- Operational readiness: Build simple runbook for common errors and hand over to SRE/ops contact.
- Deliver: Midpoint health check document and recommendations for scaling.

Days 61–90: Scale, review, and renewal prep
- Scale traffic in measured increments while validating SLOs and cost targets.
- Business review prep: compile metric dashboard, qualitative feedback from end-users, and performance/cost graphs.
- Renewal signals: capture adoption indicators (usage, expansions requested, success stories) and escalate customer to Account Exec for commercial conversations if thresholds met.
- Deliver: 90-day playbook closeout (QBR template filled), customer testimonial draft, and long-term roadmap items.

Play actions (reusable short steps)
- Template: Kickoff agenda (link to reusable doc)
- Template: Weekly status email (short bullets: wins, blockers, next steps)
- Template: Escalation email to engineering on severity 1 issues (include logs, timestamps, reproduction)
- Codified checklist: Production readiness (endpoints, auth, alerts, incident contact)

Sample weekly status email (short)
Subject: Week X — Launch status: [Customer] — Redwood
Body bullets:
- Current health: traffic %, 95th latency ms, errors %
- Completed this week: integration of X, dashboards configured, canary rollout done
- Blockers: CORS config pending, legal approval for prod data
- Next steps: ramp to 10% on Tue, run eval 2.0 on Thu

Risk register (quick table as text)
- Risk: Network restrictions (private deploy) — Impact: High — Mitigation: Pre-validate allowlists and schedule network window — Owner: Solutions Eng
- Risk: Quality regression on model update — Impact: Medium — Mitigation: Canary + rollback policy and eval set — Owner: CSM + Product
- Risk: Unexpected token costs — Impact: Medium — Mitigation: Early Optimize review and cost alerts — Owner: CSM + Customer FinOps

Health-to-renewal mapping (signals we use to prioritize renewals)
- Green (expand candidate): >80% of day-90 traffic target, positive anecdotal feedback, at least one internal champion identified.
- Yellow (monitor): Partial adoption, outstanding technical debt, commercial interest unclear.
- Red (risk): Low usage, repeated unresolved S1 incidents, cost concerns, or security blockers.

QBR (90-day) snapshot template (fill during final review)
- Executive summary: 3–4 bullets
- Usage & adoption: charts + top endpoints
- Technical health: latency, errors, incident log
- Business impact: user stories, KPI delta (if available)
- Risks & open items: top 5
- Recommended next steps: scale plan, efficiency plan, contract/expansion ask

Operational templates & trackers to attach to each customer (columns listed so you can copy into a sheet)
- Column set for tracker: customer_name, csm, account_exec, start_date, integration_owner, target_traffic, current_traffic, last_health_status, next_checkpoint_date, renewal_date, primary_risks, notes

Handoff checklist (to operations or support)
- Dashboards and alerts shared with ops
- Runbook posted in ops channel and linked in Console
- Owner for maintenance assigned and included in on-call rotation if required

Common playbook notes / lessons learned (from previous launches)
- Run a quick synthetic test with real-seeming prompts early — it surfaces tokenization and prompt engineering issues faster than production traffic.
- Keep eval sets small but representative — 30 prompts across main intents catches most regressions.
- Price sensitivity: Surface projected cost estimates in week 2 — most surprises happen from high token/session use-cases.
- Canary early, rollback fast — configure automatic fallback to lighter model variant if latency or cost spikes.

Templates to copy from (links placeholder)
- Kickoff agenda: [link]
- Weekly status email: [link]
- Integration checklist (sheet): [link]
- Eval harness (simple script): [link]

Open questions to capture in kickoff (use during first meeting)
- What are the unambiguous success metrics for this customer at day 30 and day 90?
- What internal stakeholders need access to Console or logs?
- Are there legal/compliance constraints that will affect data flow or logging?
- Is there an internal timeline (e.g., product launch) that constrains the ramp schedule?

Next steps for the CSM when using this template
1) Duplicate this doc in the customer folder and attach trackers.
2) Schedule kickoff within 48 hours.
3) Ensure Solutions Eng has all access in the first 72 hours.
4) Run week 1 synthetic test and share results in the first weekly status.

Notes to self (CSM quick tips)
- Keep communications short and outcome-focused — customers are often time-starved.
- Use metrics to lead the conversation — show how adoption correlates to product KPI.
- Track non-technical blockers (legal, procurement) with as much energy as technical ones — they often delay launch.

Document history
